en: Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Bara' ibn Azib saying: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq came to my father in his residence and bought a saddle from him, and said to Azib: "Send your son with me to carry it with me to my residence." So my father said to me: "Carry it." So I carried it, and my father went out with him to receive its payment. My father said to him: "O Abu Bakr, tell me what you two did on the night you traveled with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." He said: "Yes, we journeyed all through our night until the midday heat was at its peak and the road was deserted with no one passing along it, until a tall rock appeared before us which had shade that the sun had not yet reached. So we halted beside it. I went to the rock and leveled with my hands a place in its shade for the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to sleep, then spread a fur rug over it. Then I said: Sleep, O Messenger of Allah, and I will dust and look around for you. So he slept, and I went out to look around him. Suddenly I saw a shepherd approaching with his sheep toward the rock, desiring from it what we had desired. I met him and said: To whom do you belong, O boy? He said: To a man from the people of Medina. I said: Is there any milk in your sheep? He said: Yes. I said: Will you milk for me? He said: Yes. So he caught a ewe. I said to him: Dust the udder of hair, dust, and debris—he said: and I saw al-Bara' striking one hand against the other, dusting—so he milked for me into a wooden bowl he had a draught of milk. He said: And I had a small water skin with me to carry water for the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to drink from and make ablution. He said: So I came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and was reluctant to awaken him from his sleep, but I found him just waking up. So I poured some water onto the milk until the bottom of it cooled down. Then I said: O Messenger of Allah, drink from this milk. He said: So he drank until I was pleased. Then he said: Has the time not come to depart? I said: Yes. He said: So we set off after the sun had passed its meridian. Suraqah ibn Malik followed us—he said: while we were in hard ground—so I said: O Messenger of Allah, we have been overtaken! He said: 'Do not grieve; indeed, Allah is with us.' Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) supplicated against him, and his mare sank up to its belly, I believe. So he said: I have known that you two have prayed against me, so pray to Allah for me, and by Allah I swear to you that I will turn back those in search of you. So he prayed to Allah, and he was freed. He returned, and whenever he met anyone he would say: I have spared you this area; and he did not meet anyone except that he turned him back. He said: And he was faithful to us."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, who said: I heard Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani saying: I heard al-Bara' saying: When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came traveling from Mecca to Medina, Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum followed him. He said: So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) supplicated against him, and his mare sank into the ground. He said: "Pray to Allah for me, and I will not harm you." He said: So he prayed to Allah. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) became thirsty, and they passed by a shepherd of sheep. Abu Bakr as-Siddiq said: "So I took a bowl and milked into it a draught of milk for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), then brought it to him, and he drank until I was pleased."

Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq said: When we set out with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) from Mecca to Medina, we passed by a shepherd while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had become thirsty. He said: So I milked for him a draught of milk and brought it to him, and he drank until I was pleased.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—both saying: Affan narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: I certainly gave the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to drink with this cup of mine all kinds of drinks: honey, nabidh, water, and milk.

Muhammad ibn Sahl at-Tamimi and Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me—Abu Bakr said "informed us" and Ibn Sahl said "narrated to us"—: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Muhammad—and he is Ibn Mutarrif Abu Ghassan—informed us: Abu Hazim informed me, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: A woman from among the Arabs was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), so he instructed Abu Usayd to send for her. He sent for her and she arrived, staying in a fortress of Banu Sa'idah. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) went out until he came to her and entered upon her, and behold, there was a woman lowering her head. When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) spoke to her, she said: "I seek refuge with Allah from you." He said: "I have granted you refuge from me." They said to her: "Do you know who this is?" She said: "No." They said: "This is the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) who came to propose to you." She said: "I was too wretched for that." Sahl said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) proceeded that day until he sat in the courtyard of Banu Sa'idah, he and his companions, then he said: "Give us to drink," to Sahl. He said: So I brought out this cup for them and gave them to drink from it. Abu Hazim said: So Sahl brought out that cup for us and we drank from it. He said: Later on, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz asked him to give it as a gift, and he gifted it to him. And in the narration of Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq, he said: "Give us to drink, O Sahl."

And Muhammad ibn Sahl at-Tamimi narrated to me: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Muhammad—meaning Abu Ghassan—informed us: Abu Hazim narrated to me, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, with this hadith, and he said: "in a stone bowl; so when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) finished the meal, she macerated it and gave it to him to drink, singling him out with that."

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn Abd ar-Rahman—narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, who said: I heard Sahl saying: Abu Usayd as-Sa'idi came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and invited the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... a similar narration, but he did not say: "so when he ate, she gave it to him to drink."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz—meaning Ibn Abi Hazim—narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: Abu Usayd as-Sa'idi invited the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to his wedding banquet, and his wife that day was their servant, while she was the bride. Sahl said: Do you know what she gave the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to drink? She soaked some dates for him overnight in a bowl; so when he had eaten, she gave it to him to drink.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Anazi narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab ath-Thaqafi narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, from his mother, from A'ishah, who said: We used to prepare nabidh for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in a water skin tied at its top and having a spout at its bottom; we would prepare it in the morning and he would drink it in the evening, and we would prepare it in the evening and he would drink it in the morning.

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: al-Qasim—meaning Ibn al-Fadl al-Huddani—narrated to us: Thumamah—meaning Ibn Hazn al-Qushayri—narrated to us, who said: I met A'ishah and asked her about nabidh, so A'ishah called an Abyssinian maidservant and said: "Ask this one, for she used to prepare nabidh for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." The Abyssinian woman said: "I used to prepare nabidh for him in a water skin at night, tie it up, and hang it up; then in the morning he would drink from it."

And Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to me: Zakariyya ibn Adi narrated to us: Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Zayd, from Yahya Abu Umar an-Nakha'i, who said: Some people asked Ibn Abbas about selling wine, buying it, and trading in it. He said: "Are you Muslims?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then selling it, buying it, and trading in it are not permissible." He said: Then they asked him about nabidh, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) went out on a journey and then returned, while some of his companions had prepared nabidh in earthen jars (hanatim), hollowed stumps (naqir), and gourds (dubba'). He ordered it and it was poured out. Then he ordered a water skin, and raisins and water were placed in it at night. In the morning, he drank from it during that day of his, and through the coming night, and the next day until evening, so he drank and gave others to drink. When the next morning came, he ordered whatever remained of it to be poured out.

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir informed us, from al-A'mash, from Yahya Abu Umar, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Raisins used to be soaked to make nabidh for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in a water skin; he would drink it that day, the next day, and the day after that. When it was the evening of the third day, he would drink it and give others to drink, and if anything remained, he would pour it out.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Bakr's and Abu Kurayb's—Ishaq said "informed us" and the other two said "narrated to us"—: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Umar, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Raisins used to be soaked for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he would drink it that day, the next day, and the day after that until the evening of the third day, then he would order it and it would be served to others or poured out.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Yahya al-Bahrani, who said: They mentioned nabidh in the presence of Ibn Abbas, so he said: Nabidh used to be prepared for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in a water skin—Shu'bah said: on Sunday night (the eve of Monday)—and he would drink it on Monday and Tuesday until the Asr prayer; and if anything remained of it, he would give it to the servant to drink or pour it away.

Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Ubayd Abu Umar al-Bahrani, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas saying: Nabidh used to be prepared for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) at the beginning of the night, and he would drink it when morning came on that day, and during the following night, and the next day, and the next night, and the following day until Asr; and if anything remained, he would give it to the servant to drink or order it to be poured away.

And Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Hisham—meaning Ibn Sulayman al-Makhzumi—narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj: Musa ibn Uqbah informed me, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), a narration similar to the hadith of Ubaydullah.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abdallah ibn Numayr narrated to us (H); and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever drinks wine in this world shall not drink it in the Hereafter, unless he repents."

Abdallah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: "Whoever drinks wine in this world and does not repent of it will be deprived of it in the Hereafter and will not be given it to drink." It was said to Malik: "Did he elevate it to the Prophet?" He said: "Yes."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever drinks wine in this world will be deprived of it in the Hereafter."

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to us—both saying: Yahya—and he is al-Qattan—narrated to us, from Ubaydullah: Nafi' informed us, from Ibn Umar—he said: and I do not know it except from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—who said: "Every intoxicant is khamr (wine), and every wine is forbidden."
And Salih ibn Mismar as-Sulami narrated to us: Ma'n narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muttalib narrated to us, from Musa ibn Uqbah, with this chain of narration, a similar narration.

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to us—both from Rawh ibn Ubadah: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Musa ibn Uqbah informed me, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Every intoxicant is khamr, and every intoxicant is forbidden."

Abu ar-Rabi' al-Ataki and Abu Kamil narrated to us—both saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Every intoxicant is khamr, and every intoxicant is forbidden; and whoever drinks wine in this world and dies while addicted to it without repenting will not drink it in the Hereafter."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz—meaning ad-Darawardi—narrated to us, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir: that a man came from Jayshan—and Jayshan is from Yemen—and asked the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about a drink they drink in their land made from maize, which is called al-mizr. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Is it intoxicating?" He said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Every intoxicant is forbidden. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has a covenant for anyone who drinks intoxicants that He will give him to drink from tinat al-khabal." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is tinat al-khabal?" He said: "The sweat of the people of the Fire, or the discharge of the people of the Fire."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr an-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—all of them from Ibn Uyaynah (H); and Hasan al-Hulwani and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd: my father narrated to us, from Salih (H); and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—both saying: Abd ar-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, all of them from az-Zuhri, with this chain of narration. And in the hadith of Sufyan and Salih it does not say that he was asked about al-bit' (mead), while it is present in the hadith of Ma'mar; and in the hadith of Salih, she heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Every intoxicating drink is forbidden."

And Harmalah ibn Yahya at-Tujibi narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd ar-Rahman, that he heard A'ishah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was asked about al-bit' (mead), so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd ar-Rahman, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was asked about al-bit' (mead), so he said: "Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Abi Umar's—both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Ahwal, from Mujahid, from Abu Iyad, from Abdallah ibn Amr, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade preparing nabidh in vessels, they said: "Not all people can find skins." So he permitted them clay jars that are not varnished with pitch.

And Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu az-Zubayr narrated to us (H); and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Khaythamah informed us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: Nabidh used to be prepared for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in a water skin; but if they did not find a water skin, it was prepared for him in a stone bowl. Some of the people said to Abu az-Zubayr while I was listening: "Made of stone pots?" He said: "Made of stone pots."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Awanah informed us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abdillah: that nabidh used to be prepared for the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in a stone bowl.
